subject: Reliability incident: summary, OKR impact & QBR asks
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Armitage <julia@skyapps.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reliability incident — initial postmortem draft and OKR note

Hi team,

Attached is the first draft postmortem for the 5/26 service degradation that affected SkyApps (short RPC spikes, degraded tail latency for 35 minutes). I pulled together a concise timeline, root-cause hypothesis, and proposed mitigations; the doc also flags probable OKR implications for Q3.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- What happened: network fabric flapping in Region-1 triggered a series of failover rolls; KV cache thrash + compaction delays produced higher P99s.
- Impact: ~3.6% error-rate bump for redwood-hosted endpoints used by SkyApps; sustained elevated P99 from 14:22–14:57 UTC on 2027-05-26.
- Customer exposure: SkyApps dashboard graphs and API timeouts; they opened a support ticket (see cc).

Immediate asks for leadership/QBR prep:
1) Decide whether to include a one-line credit offer for SkyApps in next week's external communication (owner: Vivek).
2) Confirm owners for the mitigation rollouts (cache tuning + routing policy changes) and whether that work should be tagged as a Reliability OKR for Q3 (owner: Hannah + Marcus).
3) Approve final postmortem for distribution to customer + exec packet by EOD Monday.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-20270528.pdf (4 pages) — contains timeline.csv and appendix with initial measurement charts.

I'll incorporate feedback and produce a leadership-ready one-pager for the QBR pack.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Armitage <julia@skyapps.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability incident — initial postmortem draft and OKR note

Thanks Priyom — good concise draft. A few quick executive-level decisions so we can close the loop for QBR prep: 

1) Customer communication & credits: I agree we should offer a one-time account credit to SkyApps. Keep it modest and framed as goodwill for the disruption; ask Finance for amt suggestion but target ~1–2% of monthly committed spend. Priyom, can you draft the customer note once Hannah signs off on the technical section?

2) OKR impact: We should not retroactively expand current Q2 OKRs, but this should be a flagged candidate for a Reliability KR in Q3 (focused on routing resilience and KV cache safeguards). Marcus/Hannah — propose a single measurable KR (e.g., "Reduce P99 tail events due to cache thrash by 80% for Region-1 workloads").

3) QBR packet: Priyom — we need a one-slide Exec Summary and the postmortem as an appendix. Hannah — a short ownerable mitigation plan with ETA is required.

Timeline: I'll circulate a high-level note for the execs tomorrow; please send final artifacts by Monday 10:00am PT so we can build the QBR slide deck.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Reliability & Product Operations | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability incident — initial postmortem draft and OKR note

Folks — added the detailed timeline and a short mitigation plan to the draft; included the CSV timeline as an attachment. Key technical points: 
- Root cause: BGP route flaps in the colo provider caused a subset of nodes to re-establish peers; our failover heuristics over-evicted hot KV entries which tipped some inference shards into cold-cache reads.
- Why it lasted ~35m: the automated backoff for cache warm-up plus concurrent compaction jobs resulted in prolonged higher token latencies for long-context requests.

Action items (technical owners + ETA):
A) Short term (48–72h): adjust routing policy thresholds to avoid synchronized failovers (owner: SRE—Hannah) — target complete: 2027-06-02
B) Medium term (3–6w): implement a phased cache rewarm that staggers compaction and warms hot keys first (owner: Runtime — Marcus) — target complete: 2027-06-18
C) Customer remediation: customer credit recommendation and public postmortem (owner: Priyom/Vivek) — customer comms ready by 2027-06-01

Attachments: sla-timeline-20270528.csv (timing by shard), postmortem-draft-20270528.pdf.

I'll update the QBR slide-ready one-pager once we confirm the credit ask.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Site Reliability Engineering | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability incident — initial postmortem draft and OKR note

Agree with the proposed owners. A couple of additions from product/ops: 
- Customer impact assessment: estimated economic exposure for SkyApps is small (approx $1.1k in lost revenue for the window), but their trust signal matters — recommend we offer credit and a short technical Q&A session with their SREs. Priyom — happy to join the call.
- Quantifiable KR suggestion for Q3: "Achieve <1 minute median cache-rewarm for hot keys after failover events for Region-1 traffic" — this maps directly to the mitigation plan and is measurable in telemetry.

Costs and scheduling: medium-term runtime changes will require a small sprint (2 weeks of engineering time + canary validation). I'll put together a resource request for the OKR proposal doc.

Attachments: okr-impact-brief.md (one-pager with KR draft and resource estimate).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Armitage <julia@skyapps.com>, ACME Cloud Support <acme-support@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Finalized notes: actions, owner rollups, and QBR deliverables

Team — thanks for the quick turn. Closing the loop here with concrete next steps for the QBR and external comms: 

Decisions taken: 
- We will offer SkyApps a one-time credit pending Finance review (Vivek to confirm amount; Priyom to draft customer-facing note).
- We will include a Reliability KR candidate in Q3 focused on cache rewarm and routing resilience (Marcus/Hannah).
- Final postmortem and one-page exec summary will be included in the QBR appendix.

Action rollup (owner — due):
1) Priyom — Draft customer communication + schedule Q&A with SkyApps (due: 2027-06-03)
2) Vivek — Confirm credit amount with Finance and approve customer note (due: 2027-06-03)
3) Hannah — Complete routing threshold adjustments and update postmortem with verified telemetry (due: 2027-06-02) — in progress
4) Marcus — Submit OKR candidate with resource request for Q3 OKR planning (due: 2027-06-07)

I'll attach the leadership-ready one-pager to the QBR deck once Vivek signs off on the credit language. Priyom will copy the external note to Julia and ACME support when ready.

Thanks — team aligned.

Priyom
